title: Speeding-Up LULESH on HPX: Useful Tricks and Lessons Learned using a Many-Task-Based Approach
problem: Modern supercomputers' growing parallelism and heterogeneity challenge current programming models in expressing parallelism and masking latency. LULESH is used as a proxy application to evaluate how task-based frameworks can improve performance.
motivation: Task-based programming models like HPX offer enhanced scalability and better latency masking compared to traditional programming models on modern multi-core and distributed systems.
method: The authors implement LULESH (a proxy application for evaluating supercomputer performance) using HPX, a framework that breaks work into small tasks and automatically assigns each to a processor based on readiness—instead of requiring programmers to manually specify parallel regions as in OpenMP. This dynamic assignment keeps processors busy by always having work ready and hides latency (delays from slow operations). They further optimize for single-node performance on multi-core systems to achieve faster execution than OpenMP.
key_novelty: HPX's dynamic task scheduling—automatically assigning work to processors as it becomes ready—achieves 1.33x to 2.25x faster LULESH execution than OpenMP.
contributions: 1.33x-2.25x single-node speedups over OpenMP reference implementation using HPX
Optimization techniques and practical tricks for task-based HPC programming
Evaluation of HPX's effectiveness on proxy applications as middle ground between benchmarks and real applications
Research foundation for heterogeneous programming with GPUs and FPGAs using HPX

metrics.speedup: 1.33x-2.25x over OpenMP baseline (single-node, various problem sizes)

primary_theme: HPX task-based optimization for HPC proxy applications
